_headline: Corpus sources occupy distinct regions OF THE DIE, not only of embedding space. Concentrated, separated and pure, all beyond a label-permutation floor, and the effect strengthens under the frequency control.

_effect_sizes_not_just_z.why: The z scores are enormous (-106, +63) and that is mostly a statement about the floor's tightness at 1500 tokens and 200 permutations, not about how large the effect is. Reported separately so nobody reads -105 as 'huge'.
_effect_sizes_not_just_z.concentration: 4.502 vs 5.199 hops = 13.4% tighter than chance. Real, modest.
_effect_sizes_not_just_z.centroid_separation: 5.244 vs 3.850 hops = 36% further apart than chance. z=+3.53 is the WEAKEST of the three signals and it is the one steering depends on most.
_effect_sizes_not_just_z.cell_purity: 0.546 vs 0.231 = 2.36x chance. The strongest practical signal: a cell's characteristic tokens belong to a single source more than half the time, against a 23% baseline.

_the_control_that_mattered: The `content` condition excludes the 500 globally most frequent tokens. If the geography were a frequency artefact -- common tokens landing together because the placement optimised something correlated with count -- it would collapse there. Concentration z goes -93.9 -> -105.5 and purity +56.1 -> +63.4. It strengthens, which is the opposite of an artefact.
_what_this_licenses: Building the steering experiment. 'Sample within k hops of the poetry region' now has a referent: the regions exist, they are distinguishable, and their centroids are recorded in this file. It does NOT yet show that constraining generation to a region changes the text -- that is the next measurement and it can still come out null.
_what_would_still_make_this_inert: Purity of 0.55 means nearly half of a cell's characteristic tokens belong to some other source, and 110 cells for 32,000 tokens is ~291 tokens per cell. A neighbourhood may simply be too coarse to carry register even though the regions are statistically real. That is an effect-size question the steering run answers and this one cannot.
